transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been going on that brought you in today?

Hi. Yeah, um, well, I guess what brings me in is... it's these late work nights. I'm a graphic designer, and lately, the agency I work for has been taking on all these ridiculous last-minute rebrands. Like, last week I was working on this logo for a boutique pet bakery—which, honestly, who buys a twelve-dollar organic cupcake for a dog? I don't even have a dog, my landlord is super strict about pets anyway. 

But anyway, I'm up super late working, and I'll order what I tell myself is just going to be a normal dinner. But then... it just turns into this huge thing. I'll get a whole entrée, and then multiple sides, a dessert, and then I'm still going into my own kitchen for extra snacks on top of that. It's way, way more than I would ever eat if someone were actually sitting across the table from me. But since I work from home now—my apartment has this great little nook by the window that gets perfect morning light, though the Wi-Fi is honestly kind of spotty over there—I just... yeah, I end up eating all this stuff by myself.
When you find yourself eating all of that food in one sitting, does it feel like you're not in control, like you can't stop once you start?

Yeah... exactly. It's like, once I start eating, there's this specific point where I'm just watching myself. Like I'll be clicking back over to the delivery app to add more to my cart, or I'm in the kitchen opening another package... 

And actually, speaking of packages, the amount of plastic these delivery places use is just insane. Have you noticed that? I ordered from this new fusion place a couple weeks ago—right around my mom's birthday, actually. I always struggle with what to get her because she's one of those people who just buys whatever she wants, you know? But anyway, this restaurant sent every single side dish in its own heavy-duty, customized plastic tub. As a designer, I get that they want the branding to look premium, but it's so incredibly wasteful. I took a whole seminar on sustainable packaging when I was getting my bachelor's, and seeing all that plastic just makes me cringe. 

But, um... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right. The food. Yeah, I'll be opening another one of those packages, and in my head, I'm literally thinking, 'I really should stop now.' But it just feels like... I don't know, like the decision has already slipped out of my hands completely. My hands are just doing it anyway.
After these episodes of eating a large amount of food, do you ever make yourself vomit, take laxatives, go on a fast, or exercise excessively to try to control your weight or get rid of the calories?

No, no I don't do any of that. I definitely don't throw up or anything. Honestly, the thought of throwing up just... ugh. I had this horrible stomach bug back in 2019, right before I was supposed to go to this huge design conference in Austin. I was so excited for it, too, because I'd been saving up for months, and they were having this keynote speaker who did the branding for, like, half the major tech startups in the last decade. But I ended up spending the entire weekend in my hotel bathroom. It was miserable. I couldn't even look at the little complimentary mints on the pillow without feeling sick. 

And as for exercising... well, my gym membership is basically just a very expensive donation at this point. I keep meaning to go, especially since they just renovated the whole cardio section. They put in those new treadmills with the huge screens where you can pretend you're running through the Swiss Alps or whatever. My friend Sarah uses them all the time and she swears by it. She's actually training for a half marathon right now, which is crazy to me because she used to hate running. But yeah, I don't really do anything like that after I eat. I just... sit there feeling terrible about it.
Do you feel distressed or upset about these episodes of eating a large amount of food in a short period of time?

Yeah, I mean... it feels awful. I get really upset about it. It's just this overwhelming guilt that washes over me, and I just hate that I let it happen again. It's so frustrating because... well, it's like when you spend hours working on a project and then your computer just crashes before you hit save. 

Actually, that happened to me last month with this huge brochure design for a real estate client. They wanted this very specific shade of slate blue for the accents, and I swear I spent half the day just tweaking the hex codes to get it right on different monitors. Because colors look so different depending on the screen, you know? Like, Apple displays are usually a bit cooler, but if someone is looking at it on an older Dell monitor, it can look totally washed out. My first boss out of college was absolutely militant about color calibration. He used to make us run these diagnostic tests on our screens every Friday afternoon before we could leave for the weekend. It was so annoying at the time, but honestly, I kind of get it now. 

But yeah, the distress... it's definitely there. I just sit there afterward and feel really, really bad about myself.
How often do these episodes of eating a large amount of food in a short time happen?

Well, if I look back at my delivery receipts and my calendar... which I actually just had to do recently because I was trying to figure out where all my money was going. I started using this new budgeting app because the service fees on those delivery apps are just completely out of control lately. Have you seen that? They add a delivery fee, a service fee, and then sometimes a "small order" fee even if you're spending like thirty bucks! 

My friend Mark actually showed me this Excel spreadsheet he uses to track his expenses. He's an accountant, so he's super meticulous about that stuff. He color-codes every single category—which, as a designer, I obviously appreciate the impulse. But his color palette was just awful. He used this glaring neon green right next to this bright, aggressive red... it literally hurt my eyes to look at it. I actually ended up redesigning his whole spreadsheet for him just so I wouldn't get a headache if he ever showed it to me again. 

But, um... sorry, what was I saying? Oh, right, the receipts. Yeah, so when I actually look at the pattern on my calendar, there's usually at least one night every week where this happens. Sometimes more. And that specific pattern has been there for... gosh, several months now, I think.

There is no evidence of compensatory behaviors such as vomiting, laxative use, fasting, or excessive exercise. This presentation is consistent with binge-eating disorder (F50.2). No other disorders fit the described symptoms as well.
